cards.text: Joseph is still in prison, and Pharaoh’s chief cupbearer, the man he helped, has forgotten all about him. Two FULL years go by, and trust me, friend, I know what it’s like to be forgotten in the back of somewhere. Then Pharaoh, king of Egypt, has a dream.
In the dream, Pharaoh is standing beside the Nile. Seven cows, sleek and well-fed, come up from the river and start grazing among the reeds.

cards.question: After them, seven more cows come up from the Nile, and they look nothing like the first seven. These cows are ___ and ___.
In Pharaoh’s dream, the sickly, thin cows get scared of the well-fed cows and run back into the Nile.

cards.text: The thin cows DEVOUR the well-fed ones, and Pharaoh wakes up. Cows eating cows, friend, I’d be wide awake too.
He falls back asleep and dreams a second time. This time, seven heads of grain, plump and ripe, come up on one stalk.

cards.question: Then seven thin heads of grain sprout, scorched by the east wind. Remembering what the thin cows did, what do the thin heads of grain do?
Pharaoh wakes and realizes it was a dream. In the morning after those two dreams, his spirit is ___.
Pharaoh is troubled by his two dreams. Who does he summon to hear them?

answers.text: All the magicians and wise men of Egypt
The elders of Midian and Moab
The prophets of Baal and Asherah

cards.question: Pharaoh tells his dreams to Egypt’s magicians and wise men, and they explain them right away.

cards.text: Not one of them can interpret the dreams. A whole room full of Egypt’s wise men, and they’ve got NOTHING.

cards.question: Somebody near Pharaoh finally remembers a man who can interpret dreams. Who speaks up?

cards.text: The cupbearer tells Pharaoh, “Today I recall my failures.” Friend, that’s the guy answering your text two YEARS late.
He tells Pharaoh about the night in custody when he and the chief baker both had dreams. A young Hebrew there, a servant of the captain of the guard, interpreted each dream for them.

cards.question: The cupbearer says it all happened just as the young Hebrew interpreted. What happened to the cupbearer?

answers.text: He was restored to his position
He was released and sent home
He was made captain of the guard

cards.question: After hearing the cupbearer’s story, Pharaoh sends for Joseph.

cards.text: Joseph is quickly brought out of the dungeon. A shave, a change of clothes, and straight in to see the king: the fastest glow-up in all of Egypt.
Pharaoh says to him, “I had a dream, and no one can interpret it. But I have heard it said of you that when you hear a dream you can interpret it.”

cards.question: Pharaoh has heard that Joseph can interpret dreams. How does Joseph answer him?

answers.text: He says God will give the answer
He says he has done this before
He asks for his freedom first

cards.text: Pharaoh tells Joseph the dream, cows and all, and adds, “I have never seen such ugly cows in all the land of Egypt!” The man rules ALL of Egypt, and he’s still roasting the cows.

cards.question: Pharaoh tells Joseph that after the thin cows devoured the well-fed cows, the thin cows looked well-fed themselves.

cards.text: Then he tells the grain dream: seven plump heads swallowed by seven thin, scorched ones. He told the magicians, he says, and no one could explain it.

cards.question: Joseph tells Pharaoh that his two dreams have two different meanings.
Joseph says the dreams reveal to Pharaoh what ___ is about to do.

cards.text: Joseph starts decoding. The seven good cows are seven years, and the seven ripe heads of grain are seven years.

cards.question: If the good cows and the ripe grain are seven years, what are the seven thin cows and the scorched grain?

cards.text: Joseph comes back to it: God has shown Pharaoh what He is about to do. Seven years of great abundance are coming throughout the land of Egypt.

cards.question: Joseph says that once the famine comes, people will still remember the years of abundance.

cards.text: Joseph says the famine will devastate the land. It will be so severe that the good years won’t even be remembered.

cards.question: Why does Joseph say Pharaoh was given the dream in two versions?

answers.text: God decreed it and will do it shortly
So Pharaoh would remember it longer
Because the magicians missed the first one

cards.text: Twice means it’s settled, and it’s coming shortly. Friend, when God says it twice, you do NOT hit snooze.

cards.question: Now Joseph tells Pharaoh what to do about it. Who should Pharaoh look for and set over the land of Egypt?
Joseph says Pharaoh should appoint commissioners to take a ___ of Egypt’s harvest during the seven years of abundance.

cards.text: Under Pharaoh’s authority, they’ll collect the excess food from the good years and store the grain in the cities. It’s a savings account, but for grain.

cards.question: Joseph has laid out the plan to store up grain in the cities. What will all that stored food be for?

answers.text: A reserve for the famine years
Goods to trade with other nations

cards.question: Joseph says that with this reserve, the country will not perish in the famine.

cards.text: And that’s where we’ll pause, friend. Joseph just laid a whole plan in front of the king of Egypt, and believe me, this story is NOT done.
